ma_haig.text: Come in, hen, come in. Selkirk bannock, Border tart and a pie that'd stop a Reiver at forty paces. The bannock's fruit bread, and Queen Victoria is said to have liked it, so you've no excuse.
Mind the steps. The Common Riding's on, and half the town's in here wanting breakfast.

then.text: You've got them. Now off you go, and don't let a Hawick man near the colours.

else.text: Oh, you're the one the Cornet sent. The colours are in the cupboard behind the bannocks, wrapped in a tea-towel. They've been in the family for 80 years. It's a bit of a secret. We don't tell the next town.
My late husband was Cornet in '62. He rode every march and never lost the colours. He did once lose a horse, but that was a different matter.
